steps.title: Four sentences about a course that has not started yet.
steps.sub: All four are about the future. Look at the verb after the time word.

items.text: When you arrive, the instructor will check your fitness level.
I’ll call as soon as I know the dates.
Before you come, you’ll need to reserve a place.

steps.title: Look at the four sentences again.
steps.sub: When you arrive, the instructor will check …
steps.prompt: Which half has the present tense?
options: The half with when / as soon as / before / until.
The half with will, because it is about the future.
Both halves have will, because both are about the future.
steps.answer: The half with when / as soon as / before / until.
steps.why: After a time word, English uses a present tense even when the meaning is future — exactly like after if.

steps.title: Talking about the future after a time word
steps.html:
Time word + Present Simplewill / won’t + base form
When you arrive,the instructor will check your fitness.
As soon as I know the dates,I’ll call you.
Before you come,you’ll need to reserve a place.
After the course finishes,we’ll send you a certificate.
Until everybody is here,we won’t start.

The time words are when, as soon as, before, after, until, once, while.

After them, use a present tense. Never say when you will arrive in this kind of sentence.

Until means “up to that moment”. The result half is usually negative: We won’t start until he arrives.

As soon as means “immediately after”. It is stronger than when: I’ll ring you as soon as I land.

This is the same rule you met after if in the last lesson.

steps.title: You are going to hear someone calling about an outdoor training course.
steps.sub: What do you think they will ask about? There is no wrong answer here.

options.label: how fit you need to be

steps.title: Listen to part 1: do I need to be fit?
steps.prompt: What is the caller worried about?
options: That she is not fit enough for the course.
That the course is too expensive.
That the dates are wrong.
steps.answer: That she is not fit enough for the course.

steps.title: Listen to part 1: do I need to be fit?
steps.prompt: Does she need to go to the gym first?
options: No — the course is for anybody.
Yes, for at least a month.
Yes, but only twice a week.
steps.answer: No — the course is for anybody.

steps.title: Listen to part 1: do I need to be fit?
steps.prompt: What will happen when she arrives?
options: The instructor will check her fitness level and divide the group in two.
She will take a written test about the course and the equipment.
She will pay for the whole course before anything else happens.
steps.answer: The instructor will check her fitness level and divide the group in two.

steps.title: Listen to part 2: the weather and the booking.
steps.prompt: What will happen if it rains or snows?
options: The course will still take place outside.
The course will move indoors for the day.
The course will be cancelled until spring.
steps.answer: The course will still take place outside.

steps.title: Listen to part 2: the weather and the booking.
steps.prompt: Does she need to book a place?
options: Yes — she will need to reserve a place before she comes.
No, she can just turn up on the morning of the course.
Only if she is a complete beginner rather than intermediate.
steps.answer: Yes — she will need to reserve a place before she comes.
